fields.name: companyLocationTab
fields.label: Ship To / Bill To
fields.sourceQuote: 1.  On the Company Locations page, select the Ship To or Bill To tab.
fields.notes: Tab selector on the Company Locations page. Both tab names are documented verbatim in a single sentence in delete-a-shipping-or-billing-address-ae7aef28.md and again in export-shipping-or-billing-addresses-59f051b2.md, so this is an enumerated pair from the corpus, not a completed toggle. The tab is emitted here because it is the context that selects the field set: the 12-row field table is written for the Ship To tab ('select the Ship To tab' / 'Add New Ship To Location window') yet two of its rows are bill-to-only (VAT ID) or bill-to-side-only (Add address as a Ship To Location as well), so the per-tab field sets are NOT identical.

fields.name: locationName
fields.label: Name
fields.sourceQuote: A unique name that identifies a specific address.
fields.notes: Required. Row 1 of the 12-row 'Field / Description/Comments' table in the Add New Ship To Location window. Note in the same cell: 'This is the value that displays when choosing a default shipping address in Profile > Profile Settings > Invoice Preferences, and when creating a policy and selecting the value for Bill To.' Tip in the same cell: 'The system searches for your location by using the Name value.' No length limit documented for this field on the page (the PO import 210/220 Name column is capped at 100 characters, but that is the import file, not the page).

fields.name: addressCode
fields.label: Address Code
fields.sourceQuote: This is the external identifier used by the customer's financial system to identify a specific address.
fields.notes: Required. Row 2. Note in the same cell: 'This value is identical to the External ID field used in the Bill To and Ship To record sets of the Purchase Order import.' Also the reactivation key on delete (a removed address 'can be reactivated by entering the same Address Code'), the Employee Import 360-record key for default shipping assignment, and the Peppol match key. No length limit documented for the on-page field.

fields.name: address1
fields.label: Address 1
fields.sourceQuote: Address 1 of the complete address.
fields.notes: Required. Row 3. No length limit documented for the on-page field (the PO import 210/220 column is 'Maximum 255 characters').

fields.name: address2
fields.label: Address 2
fields.sourceQuote: Address 2 of the complete address.
fields.notes: Optional. Row 4.

fields.name: address3
fields.label: Address 3
fields.sourceQuote: Address 3 of the complete address.
fields.notes: Optional. Row 5.

fields.name: city
fields.label: City
fields.sourceQuote: The city within which the address resides.
fields.notes: Required. Row 6.

fields.name: postalCode
fields.label: Postal Code
fields.sourceQuote: The postal code of the address.
fields.notes: Required. Row 7.

fields.name: countryCode
fields.label: Country Code
fields.sourceQuote: The code of the country associated with the address.
fields.notes: Required. Row 8. Note in the same cell: 'If you are using the import template to import company locations, you must use 2 character ISO code.' The corpus does NOT enumerate the accepted values for this on-page field and does not point it at any list. The 249-row Country Code List catalog in country-code-list-8b3e2eda.md is documented for a different scope ('the country code list that you use when creating the vendor import file') and is therefore recorded as an UNWIRED value set, not as this field's validValues. fieldType left unknown: the corpus never states whether this is a text box or a list, and the guide revision history dated March 18, 2016 notes only that the State/Province field 'has changed to a list', not Country Code.

fields.name: stateProvince
fields.label: State/Province
fields.sourceQuote: The state or province within which the address resides.
fields.notes: Optional on the Company Locations page (row 9). CONTRADICTION with the PO import: both the 210 and 220 record formats mark State/Province Required? = Y. The guide revision history dates the page-side change: September 9, 2016 'State/Province field now an optional field', and March 18, 2016 'Updated images to show that the State/Province field has changed to a list when creating a new ship-to or bill-to address' — the list contents are never enumerated in this corpus, so validValues is empty and fieldType is left unknown rather than asserted as a dropdown.

fields.name: emailAddress
fields.label: Email Address
fields.sourceQuote: The email address of the contact at the company location.
fields.notes: Optional. Row 10. Added per the guide revision history dated April 14, 2018 ('the addition of the email address field to the add and modify ship-to and bill-to windows'). Consumed by the Purchase Order Header 'Use Email as Bill-To' field configured on Forms and Fields — see dependencyCandidates.

fields.name: vatId
fields.label: VAT ID
fields.sourceQuote: The VAT of the buyer.
fields.notes: Optional. Row 11. Note in the same cell: 'This is only applicable on the bill-to address and required by some European countries.' This is the row that makes the Ship To and Bill To tab field sets non-identical. Added per the guide revision history dated September 9, 2016 ('VAT ID field in bill-to address'). The corpus does not say which European countries make it required.

fields.name: addAddressAsShipToLocationAsWell
fields.label: Add address as a Ship To Location as well
fields.sourceQuote: Select (enable) this check box if you would like to populate the ship-to address with the same address information as the bill-to address.
fields.notes: Optional. Row 12, the last row of the table. Explicitly typed as a check box by the source ('this check box'), so 'checkbox' here is documented, not inferred. Functionally a bill-to-side control (it copies the bill-to address into a ship-to record), although the table it lives in is introduced under 'select the Ship To tab' — the corpus does not resolve that tension. No default state is documented; no on/off value labels are enumerated, so validValues stays empty.

valueSetCandidates.context: UNWIRED BY DESIGN. The complete 249-row Code / Country / Notes catalog from country-code-list-8b3e2eda.md. Its documented scope, verbatim, is: 'The following lists the country code list that you use when creating the vendor import file.' It is NOT documented as the value list for the Company Locations Country Code field, and the Company Locations Country Code cell says only 'If you are using the import template to import company locations, you must use 2 character ISO code' without pointing at any list. Wiring this catalog to countryCode would be an inference, so appliesToField is deliberately left empty. ENCODING: each value is '<Code> — <Country>' with the source's Notes column, where non-empty, appended in square brackets; 13 of the 249 rows carry such a note. Country names are ALL CAPS in the source and are reproduced verbatim including diacritics (ÅLAND ISLANDS, SAINT BARTHÉLEMY). Codes must be entered in capitals: 'It is important that you use capital letters (ALL CAPS) for the country code.'

valueSetCandidates.context: The two tabs of the Company Locations page, enumerated together in one sentence.
valueSetCandidates.sourceQuote: 1.  On the Company Locations page, select the Ship To or Bill To tab.
valueSetCandidates.notes: Both names come from a single documented sentence, so this is an enumerated pair rather than a completed toggle. The same pairing recurs verbatim in export-shipping-or-billing-addresses-59f051b2.md. Note the label drift across the corpus: the tabs are 'Ship To' / 'Bill To' but the windows they open are 'Add New Ship To Location' and 'Modify Ship To Location', the import window is 'Import Ship To Locations', and prose elsewhere uses the hyphenated forms 'ship-to' / 'bill-to' and 'Ship-To' / 'Bill-To'. The corpus never shows an 'Add New Bill To Location' window title.

contradictions.topic: State/Province requiredness: optional on the Company Locations page, required in the PO import records that populate the same addresses
contradictions.readingA: Company Locations page field table marks State/Province '(Optional)' — add-a-shipping-or-billing-address-3b51c816.md; corroborated by the guide revision history entry dated September 9, 2016, 'State/Province field now an optional field'.
contradictions.readingB: Both PO import address record formats mark State/Province Required? = Y, Definition 'Maximum 255 characters' — records 210 and 220. Since these imports create and update the very same Company Locations rows, the two rules disagree about the same stored value. Not reconciled here.

contradictions.topic: Country Code column definition differs between the 210 and the 220 record, which are otherwise field-for-field identical
contradictions.readingA: Record type 210 (Bill-to): Country Code Definition is '2 characters'.
contradictions.readingB: Record type 220 (Ship-to): Country Code Definition is 'Maximum 2 characters'. The External ID and Name Description text also differ between the two files ('This is the external identifier used by the customer to identify a particular address.' / 'An optional name that can be used to identify a particular address.' vs 'A unique value supplied by the customer to identify a particular address.' / 'An optional name that can be given to the address.'). Recorded per-file rather than merged.

contradictions.topic: Country Code enumeration for Company Locations: no list is documented, and the only 249-row catalog in the corpus is scoped to a different import
contradictions.readingA: The Company Locations Country Code cell states only a format rule: 'If you are using the import template to import company locations, you must use 2 character ISO code.' No values are enumerated and no list is referenced.
contradictions.readingB: country-code-list-8b3e2eda.md enumerates 249 codes but scopes itself verbatim to 'the country code list that you use when creating the vendor import file'. The corpus never joins the two. Recorded as an unwired value set rather than resolved.

contradictions.topic: Three different external guide names for what appears to be one Company Locations document, none of which is present in this corpus
contradictions.readingA: 'Concur Invoice: Company Locations Setup Guide' (understand-and-use-company-locations-377ff23e.md, and again in create-an-invoice-with-tax-validation-a515e7a3.md).
contradictions.readingB: 'Concur Invoice: Company Locations User Guide' (set-a-default-shipping-and-billing-address-f772bed1.md, twice) and 'Shared: Locations Setup Guide' (provide-a-location-for-the-tax-service-6ba2cb41.md).

contradictions.topic: Navigation rendering to the same page varies across four topics
contradictions.readingA: 'Company Locations is accessible from the Invoice Processing Admin menu.' with numbered steps 'Go to Administration > Invoice.' then 'Select Company Locations (left menu).' — a 4-hop path in prose, a 3-hop path in the steps.
contradictions.readingB: 'Click Administration > Invoice, and then click Company Locations' (set-a-default-shipping-and-billing-address-f772bed1.md); the backslash-escaped no-space form in understand-and-use-company-locations-377ff23e.md; and the alias-rooted 'To add shipping information, click Invoice Admin > Company Locations.' (provide-a-location-for-the-tax-service-6ba2cb41.md).

contradictions.topic: Three near-identical 'change ship-to / bill-to address' topics with distinct loios describe genuinely different controls
contradictions.readingA: change-ship-to-or-bill-to-address-18a4dbb6.md: purchase REQUEST, 'In the Ship To or Bill To section, click Change.', then click the Ship To or Bill To field directly — no named window. change-ship-to-address-564e516a.md: purchase request PROCESSOR, ship-to only, 'click the Change link'.
contradictions.readingB: change-ship-to-or-bill-to-address-2c926795.md: purchase ORDER, 'In the Ship To or Bill To section, click Edit.', and a named 'Change Address window' with separate ship-to and bill-to renderings. So these are NOT a gerund/imperative republish pair — the object (request vs order vs processor view) and the control (Change link vs Edit) genuinely differ. All three are END-USER controls on purchase requests/orders, not Company Locations page controls, so none is emitted as a field here.
